analysis:
Reviewed the release doc update, the mlx-swift-lm submodule bump, and three Swift provider files.

1. docs/operations/provider-release.md (head): documentation only. Prepares 0.9.21 and says it pins merged mlx-swift-lm #305. Release pipeline text is otherwise consistent with the existing official-identity, revocation and App Attest model. No security control is changed, and the doc claims no new activation.

2. libs/mlx-swift-lm: the submodule pointer moves from 53d9647 to 5c2ff51. The submodule contents are not supplied, so the ordinary-request retirement API cannot be reviewed. Coverage limit: any change to cancellation, KV or request retirement affecting T-010, T-028 or T-041 is unexamined.

3. EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift: EnginePrefillReceipt gains measurementPurpose (default .serving) and calibrationCell. The comment says a delayed calibration callback must never become serving work. The consumers of these fields (the calibration policy and the bridge code that reads receipts) are not in this batch, so the enforcement is unverified. The type EngineMeasurementPurpose and ModelCalibrationPolicy.Cell are defined elsewhere. Next pass should check that take()/observe paths honor measurementPurpose, so that calibration samples cannot feed the serving deadline-rate evidence that the coordinator uses.

4. EngineV2Bridge+CalibrationPrompt.swift: rename mimoCalibrationPrompt to modelCalibrationPrompt. The body is unchanged. It uses a built-in synthetic prompt, never customer data, so A-001 is unaffected. Callers must be updated elsewhere.

5. EngineV2Bridge+Lifecycle.swift line 161: rename cancelMimoCalibration to cancelModelCalibration in shutdown(). Calibration task cancellation and await ordering are unchanged (cancelled before engine drain, awaited at line 173).

No concrete security regression is found in the supplied code. Open question: calibration for ordinary and block engines runs without a customer job, so GPU/KV use and cache side effects (T-041 prefix cache donation by synthetic prompts, T-029) are not visible here.
